To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute myocardial infarcts can be successfully treated and the mortality can be reduced to 5% or less if all patients with acute coronary syndromes are treated according to an integrated protocol.

(a) early diagnosis is the most effective measure to reduce mortality; (b) the best treatment is reperfusion of the infarcted area; (c) the best time to reperfuse the infarct is the earliest possible; (d) the best way to do this is to use thrombolytic drugs.
the acute phase of coronary artery disease has been brought within the realm of modern medicine and is no longer the "black hole" of the past.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (a) the early diagnosis of acute coronary attack and its differentiation from other conditions; (b) the development of an integrated programme of surveillance, treatment and rehabilitative procedures; (c) the development of new therapeutic approaches such as the application of antiarrhythmic agents and myocardial revascularization in the acute stage.
the early diagnosis and treatment of acute myocardial infarcts.
the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, and the application of new technologies in cardiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mortality rate of myocardial infarcts has been reduced to 1/3 in 10 years and the morbidity to 1/2 in 10 years.
acute myocardial infarcts have become an acute medical condition which, in most instances, can be treated effectively.
acute myocardial infarctions can now be treated with the best results ever.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prognosis of myocardial infarctions has improved significantly in recent years.
acute myocardial infarcts are now curable diseases.
acute coronary attack has changed from an acute fatal disease to a chronic disease which can be successfully treated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acute myocardial infarcts are not only a medical but also a surgical problem.
acute myocardial infarcts are not a disease to be left to the mercy of fate but can be treated with success by a concerted effort of the medical profession.
a large proportion of patients with acute myocardial infarcts survive the acute stage, and that the majority of these patients can be expected to return to a normal life after adequate treatment.
